review_notes: Read the whole file and DFinsupp.prod in BigOperators. Most proofs use public API (mk_injective, support_mk_subset, mk_of_mem, notMem_support_iff). The clearest fragility is card_pi, where the statement and proof depend on an accidental NatCast-to-function coercion. Secondary: mem_dfinsupp_iff uses a bare `dsimp` to expose the internals of DFinsupp.mk. I did not compile anything.

findings.excerpt: exact Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => by simp only [Pi.natCast_apply, Nat.cast_id]
findings.problem: `DFinsupp.prod` expects `g : ∀ i, β i → γ`. Here `fun i ↦ #(f i)` has type `ℕ` in the body, so Lean elaborates it through a `NatCast (Finset (α i) → ℕ)` coercion (the Pi natCast instance). The statement therefore means `(↑#(f i) : Finset (α i) → ℕ) (f i)`. The proof only works by undoing this coercion with `Pi.natCast_apply, Nat.cast_id`. A routine change to the elaboration, coercion instances or the simp-set of those lemmas would break both the statement and the proof. It also hides that the intended statement is `∏ i ∈ f.support, #(f i)`.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemma with an explicit function, `f.prod fun i s ↦ #s`, or directly as `∏ i ∈ f.support, #(f i)`. Then the proof is `card_dfinsupp _ _`, or `rw [pi, card_dfinsupp]` followed by `rfl`. This removes the dependence on `Pi.natCast_apply` and `Nat.cast_id`.
findings.benefit: The statement says what it means. The proof no longer depends on an incidental coercion or on simp lemmas that undo it. Users can rewrite with `card_pi` without a stray cast appearing in the goal.

evidence.excerpt:
(g : ∀ i, β i → γ) : γ :=
  ∏ i ∈ f.support, g i (f i)

findings.excerpt:
ext i
    dsimp
    exact ite_eq_left_iff.2 fun hi => (notMem_support_iff.1 fun H => hi <| h.1 H).symm
findings.problem: The reverse direction uses a bare `dsimp` to expose the internal definition of `DFinsupp.mk`, which it unfolds to an `ite` on membership in `s`. It then closes the goal with `ite_eq_left_iff` against that exact shape. If `DFinsupp.mk` or its coercion simp-normal form changes (for example a different decidability instance or a `dite`), `dsimp` and the `exact` break. The forward direction already uses the public lemmas `mk_of_mem` and `support_mk_subset` instead.
findings.proposed_change: Prove equality pointwise with the public API. After `ext i`, `by_cases hi : i ∈ s`. Use `mk_of_mem hi` in the positive case. In the negative case use `mk_of_notMem` (if available, otherwise `notMem_support_iff` with `support_mk_subset`) and `notMem_support_iff.1 (mt h.1 hi)`. This replaces `dsimp` and the `ite` match with named lemmas.
findings.benefit: The proof depends on the stable `mk_of_mem` / `mk_of_notMem` interface instead of the unfolded `mk` body. It also mirrors the forward direction, so a reader sees one consistent mechanism.
